DOT Order 1351.41 (AI Policy) effective 08/26/2026 establishes department-wide AI governance. The policy explicitly encourages AI adoption and establishes the NETT Council as AI Governance Board, a CDAIO, AI use case inventory, and risk management processes. The AI Accelerator Roadmap (OPSLAB, ART Network, TrAIN) provides secure environments for AI development. Detailed Generative AI Use Guidance is described as 'in final stages of development.' The policy applies to all Operating Administrations. No explicit contractor-binding language found in the department-level policy text; contractors are not named as covered parties.

Searched fhwa.dot.gov, highways.dot.gov, and the USDOT AI policy portal. Found extensive AI research programs (EAR Program, AI Deployment COE, FHWA-HRT-25-020 technical reports) but no FHWA-specific AI acceptable-use policy or employee guidance on AI tool use. The AI Deployment COE is a resource body for external stakeholders, not an internal use policy. FHWA inherits USDOT 1351.41 (governance-focused, ENCOURAGE at department level) but has no operative AI use policy of its own. Contractors performing FHWA work are not bound by any FHWA-specific AI policy.

FAA Notice 1370.52 establishes interim GAI policy effective 03/23/2025. The policy explicitly applies to all employees AND contractors. It permits GAI use with guardrails: supervisor approval required, only ESB-approved software may be used, SUI/CNSI prohibited from external GAI tools, all outputs must be reviewed for accuracy before publishing, and misuse must be reported. Contractors must discuss GAI use with their CO/COR and adhere to the same restrictions. NOTE: This Notice shows a cancellation date of 03/23/2026 and is listed as 'Cancelled' on the FAA Orders page; no replacement use policy was located during this research. FAA also references an 'FAA AI Strategy' for broader AI use beyond GAI. FAA inherits USDOT 1351.41 as a DOT Operating Administration.

entity: USACE Civil Works (U.S. Army Corps of Engineers)
notes: USACE Civil Works Memorandum 'Ethical and Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Planning Programs and Studies' (CECW-P, 3 April 2026, signed by Eric L. Bush, Chief of Civil Works Planning and Policy). The memo establishes eight guiding principles: Mission-Driven, Human Control, Transparency, Reliability & QA, Bias Avoidance, Data Stewardship, Cybersecurity, Accountability. It permits AI as a decision-support tool only, with human planners retaining full responsibility. Prohibits AI for final statutory compliance determinations, bypassing model certification, or fabricating data. Approved tools include CoPilot, Army Vantage, AskSage, and the uPoP chatbot. The memo applies to USACE Civil Works planners; contractors are not explicitly named as covered parties, though non-federal sponsors are mentioned in the context of AI not replacing commitments to them.

MTA has no standalone AI-specific policy or Acceptable Use Policy. The agency actively deploys AI across multiple programs (TrackInspect predictive maintenance with Google Public Sector, OMNY AI chatbot, AI-based weapons detection pilot, AI track intrusion detection RFI, AI-enabled fare gates) and the Capital Program Committee's February 2026 minutes reference integrating AI tools into project management systems. However, no AI governance framework, AI-specific procurement terms, or employee-facing AI use policy was located on mta.info. WMATA has a published AI Terms Annex (Sept 2025, updated March 2026) incorporated into its Standard IT Terms and Conditions, explicitly binding all contractors. The Annex defines AI Technology broadly (deep learning, ML, neural networks, transformers, LLMs, reinforcement learning), requires contractors to maintain a documented AI Program with risk management, prohibits use of WMATA data to train AI models, mandates bias/discrimination testing, and includes indemnification. The March 2026 Board Digital & AI Ecosystem Acceleration update confirms 'Digital/AI ecosystem acceleration' is a Strategic Transformation Plan priority, with 'Foundational Data Security and Responsible AI' workstreams including 'AI Policy,' 'Data Warehousing,' and 'AI Security.' The Board presentation lists AI use cases across procurement, video operations, maintenance, customer experience, frontline digitization, and supply chain. Contractor-binding: explicit.

entity: LA Metro (Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority)
notes: LA Metro has no standalone AI-specific policy. The Board-approved Bias-Free Policing Policy and Public Safety Analytics Policy provide governance for AI in safety/surveillance contexts (including algorithmic audits, transparency, bias mitigation, alignment with White House AI Bill of Rights). However, these are not agency-wide AI policies — they govern law enforcement and public safety analytics specifically. No AI-specific Acceptable Use Policy, AI procurement terms, or overarching AI governance framework was located on metro.net. The LA City ITA published a 'Los Angeles A.I. Roadmap' (June 2024) but that applies to City of LA departments, not LA Metro (a separate county authority). MBTA inherits the Massachusetts Executive Office of Technology Services and Security (EOTSS) Enterprise Use and Development of Generative AI Policy (effective Jan 31, 2025, Document ID AI.001). MBTA is an executive branch agency under MassDOT and is bound by EOTSS enterprise policies. The policy establishes mandatory guardrails: continuous fact-checking and human verification of AI outputs, disclosure/labeling of AI-generated content, procurement approval via the Commonwealth CTO before acquiring AI software/services, an AI Catalog of approved solutions, bias identification/mitigation across the AI lifecycle, and compliance with enterprise security policies. The policy applies to all personnel including contractors, consultants, vendors, and interns. MBTA's July 2025 Safety Committee minutes confirm AI is being used (audit plans, video monitoring) with staff approaching use cautiously and emphasizing human redundancy. Contractor-binding: explicit.
